faqs.a: Tilt-shift is a photography effect that keeps one horizontal band of the photo sharp while blurring the areas above and below it. The shallow-focus look tricks the brain into seeing a miniature model instead of a real scene.
The tool renders a blurred copy of the photo, draws the sharp original underneath, then overlays the blurred version on the top and bottom regions with a gradient mask. The middle band stays sharp.
faqs.q: How does this tool create the effect?

faqs.a: Put the focus band over the main subject — usually slightly below the vertical center for landscapes. A band of 20–40% of the image height looks most natural.
faqs.q: Where should I place the focus band?

faqs.a: Feather controls how gradually the blur fades into the sharp band. Low feather gives a hard edge like a real tilt-shift lens; high feather gives a dreamy gradual transition.
Yes, but gently: small amounts add atmosphere. Too much blur washes out the top and bottom completely, which can look artificial.
faqs.q: Can I blur the whole background?

faqs.a: No. The image is processed with the canvas API inside your browser.

tilt-shift-effect.formula:
band top = focusY − bandHeight ÷ 2   (all in % of image height)
band bottom = focusY + bandHeight ÷ 2

sharp where bandTop < y < bandBottom; blurred elsewhere,
with a feather gradient softening the transition.
howTo: Upload a photo — cityscapes and scenes shot from above work best.
Drag the focus position to the band you want to keep sharp.
Set the band height: narrower bands look more miniature.
Increase the blur for a stronger effect and feather for a softer transition.
keyFacts: Tilt-shift mimics the shallow depth of field of a tilt-shift camera lens.
A sharp horizontal band surrounded by blur reads as a miniature scene to the eye.
The effect works by compositing a blurred copy over the top and bottom regions.
A gradient mask feathers the transition between sharp and blurred areas.
Photos taken from a high angle sell the miniature illusion best.
All compositing happens locally with canvas layers and gradient masks.

tilt-shift-effect.workedExample:
You upload a 1200 × 800 city photo and set focus = 60%, band = 30%, blur = 8 px, feather = 25%.

Focus line y = 60% × 800 = 480 px.
Band top = 480 − (30% × 800) ÷ 2 = 480 − 120 = 360 px.
Band bottom = 480 + 120 = 600 px.
Feather = 25% × 800 = 200 px of soft transition.

The 240 px band from y = 360 to y = 600 stays tack sharp while the sky above and street below melt into blur — the city reads as a tiny model.
